title: Probatorium results document
description: v5.4 schema for probatorium per-run results files. Additive over v4: every v4 field is still present, plus environment, benchmark_config, compile_options, latency_at_slo, hdr_histogram_b64, validation_results, soak_summary, (v5.2) per-(adapter, scenario) server resources, (v5.3) per-server cell_statuses recording cells that did not produce a real number (not_applicable / dnf) so they are not ranked as 0-RPS also-rans, and (v5.4) the 'suspect' status (cell ran but its loadgen error ratio blew the scenario's error budget — data kept, integrity flagged) plus per-server cell_run_statuses preserving the per-run outcome sequence so an OK rerun can never erase prior non-OK evidence. A v4 reader sees a strict superset of the fields it knows. Both the in-process runner and the cluster mage Bench path emit this single canonical shape.

schema_version.description: Schema generation tag. v5.x readers parse 4.x and 5.x; future readers will gate on the major version.

host_arch_pair.description: Lowercased <os>_<arch> tag (e.g. linux_amd64) — the canonical key for cross-host artifact catalogues.

kernel_sysctls_applied.description: Sorted list of key=value pairs the ansible role wrote before the run started.

sut_env.description: KEY=VALUE environment overrides the bench merged into the SUT process (v5.9+, celeris#585), so an A/B arm is identifiable from this file alone. Omitted when none were passed.

nic_irq_placement.description: The NIC interrupt placement the SUT host ran under (v5.21, goceleris/celeris#1036): the vector name, the one CPU it was pinned to, and per IRQ the smp_affinity_list / effective_affinity_list before and after. Omitted when the host applies none. A changed placement changes comparability.

binding.description: Which check tied the vector to the interface: every IRQ listed under /sys/class/net/<iface>/device/msi_irqs, or the vector name starting with <iface>-.

at_end.description: The same record, read back after the last cell (no write). verified=false when the vector left its CPU during the run.

at_end_error.description: The end-of-run readback's message when it failed.

arch_exclusion.description: Arch-exclusion verdict of a BENCH_TARGET=both run (v5.22, probatorium#442), stamped into both arches' documents at merge time. Omitted on single-arch runs; on a document from a both-arch run, absent means the arches ran concurrently with nothing excluded (written before 5.22).

policy.description: heavy: no heavy cell of one arch overlaps a heavy cell of the other. all: no cells overlap. off: nothing excluded.

cell_order.description: The order this arch walked each column's cells.

heavy_light_overlaps.description: Pairs where exactly one window is heavy: the shared load a heavy pass ran under.

violations.description: Window pairs the policy forbids that intersect. Must be 0 for the document to publish.

load_windows.description: Every interval this arch's runner drove load through the loadgen host, one per saturation pass and rated pass (v5.22, probatorium#442). Times are the runner's clock on the loadgen host. Not part of the published summary.json.

ratedPass.description: One rated pass of one run of a cell (v5.24). Counts that are absent are zero when status is present.

run.description: Position of the run among the cell's runs that carried rated data.

fraction.description: Fraction of the cell's saturation rate this pass offered.

target_rps.description: Offered rate. Zero on a not_run pass whose target was never computed.

p99.description: Coordinated-omission-corrected p99, nanoseconds. Zero for a pass that is not ok.

status.description: ok: counted in latency_at_slo and the headline. skipped: the pass ran and produced no usable result. not_run: the pass never started.

detail.description: Error text where there is one.

achieved_rps.description: loadgen requests per second over the measured window.

achieved_ratio.description: achieved_rps / target_rps. Below 1 is load loadgen never sent: the p99 is then the pass's backlog, not the server's latency.

shortfall_requests.description: target x duration - requests - errors; negative when over-delivered.

rated_mode_p99_at_target_rps.description: Per-scenario merged-across-runs P99 latency, encoded as time.Duration (nanoseconds).

rated_headline_target_rps.description: Per-scenario target RPS that rated_mode_p99_at_target_rps was read at (v5.24, probatorium#441): the highest target among the KEPT rated passes. It is the cell's top fraction only if that pass was kept. Omitted for a cell with no kept pass.

rated_passes.description: Per-scenario list of every rated pass of every run of the cell, kept or not (v5.24, probatorium#441): the rate loadgen achieved, its errors, and for a pass that is not ok a status and a reason. latency_at_slo and rated_mode_p99_at_target_rps are built from the passes with status 'ok' only; a record without status comes from a runner that predates 5.24 (only target_rps and p99 were recorded, and it was kept). Omitted for a cell with no rated record. Older readers ignore the field.

latency_at_slo.description: Outer key: scenario name. Inner key: SLO threshold in milliseconds. Inner value: max sustained RPS at which merged P99 stays below the SLO.

hdr_histogram_b64.description: Per-scenario merged-across-runs HdrHistogram (V2-compressed base64). Empty string allowed when a loadgen build did not emit a per-run histogram.

connect_errors.description: Per-scenario dial/handshake-failure subset of the loadgen error total (additive within v5.4; loadgen Result.ConnectErrors). A scenario whose errors are ~all connect-class was unreachable, not misbehaving. Optional; omitted when zero, including for every pre-ConnectErrors loadgen build. Older readers ignore the field.

resources.description: Per-scenario server-side resource aggregate (RSS/CPU/GC/FD), keyed by scenario name. Optional (v5.2+); per-metric leaves are nullable so non-Go competitors expose RSS/CPU/FD only. On the cluster path this is the COLUMN-WIDE aggregate (one mpstat/observer per column pass) stamped onto every scenario — see scenario_resources for the per-scenario window.

scenario_resources.description: Per-scenario WINDOW of the same raw sidecar (v5.9+, celeris#585), keyed by scenario name: the column's 1 Hz mpstat + observer series sliced to the scenario's own runner window (started_at + warmup .. completed_at) and summarised on their own, with the slice bounds and sample counts in `window`. Absent for a scenario whose window caught no sample (no data, never zero). This, not `resources`, is the per-cell CPU number.

cell_statuses.description: Per-scenario outcome for cells this adapter did NOT produce a clean number for, keyed by scenario name (v5.3+). Value is 'not_applicable' (route/protocol unimplemented), 'dnf' (dial/port/crash/timeout) or 'suspect' (v5.4+: the cell completed but its loadgen error ratio blew the scenario's error budget). A not_applicable/dnf scenario is deliberately absent from saturation_mode_rps / latency_at_slo / hdr_histogram_b64 — it did not run, so it is never ranked as a 0-RPS row; a suspect scenario keeps its headline numbers next to the flag. 'ok' is documented as a value for completeness but never emitted (OK cells carry real numbers in the headline maps instead). Optional; omitted when every cell for this adapter ran. Older readers ignore the field.

cell_run_statuses.description: Per-scenario per-run outcome sequence in execution order (v5.4+), keyed by scenario name, emitted only when at least one run of the cell came back non-OK. Preserves the evidence of every run so an OK rerun can never erase a prior crash from the record. Optional; older readers ignore the field.

resourceStats.description: Server-side resource aggregate for one (adapter, scenario) cell (probatorium#154).

window.description: Set only on a per-scenario slice (v5.9+): the [start, end] the raw series was cut to (UTC, inclusive at 1 s) and how many samples of each kind fell inside — the denominators behind the summary means.

resourceSummary.description: Scalar headline of a cell's resource usage. Every metric is nullable: non-Go competitors leave goroutine/GC/heap null.

mean_soft_pct.description: Mean mpstat %soft (softirq) over the window (v5.9+, per-scenario slices only).

sut_process_cpu_pct.description: SUT process utime+stime over the window as percent of ONE core (v5.9+, per-scenario slices only; 3200 = all 32 cores). Needs an observer that records cpu ticks.

mean_iowait_pct.description: Mean mpstat %iowait over the rows that carried the column (v5.17+, celeris#585). Null when the cpu.log had no %iowait column.

mean_cpu_ex_iowait_pct.description: Mean of (100 - %idle - %iowait) over the same rows as mean_iowait_pct: host CPU that was executing, comparable across io_uring and epoll columns (v5.17+, celeris#585). mean_cpu_pct stays the mean over every CPU row.

zc_sends_submitted.description: SUT engine SEND_ZC submits over the window: the delta between the first and last observer samples that published the counter (v5.17+, celeris#585). Null unless at least two samples published it and it never decreased; 0 is a reading.

zc_notifs.description: SUT engine SEND_ZC notifications over the window (v5.17+, celeris#585); same delta rule as zc_sends_submitted.

inline_bytes.description: Bytes the SUT's detached streams wrote with a raw write(2), never zero-copy, over the window (v5.17+, celeris#585); same delta rule as zc_sends_submitted.

ring_bytes.description: Bytes the SUT's io_uring ring sent over the window (v5.17+, celeris#585); same delta rule as zc_sends_submitted.

bytes_written.description: Total bytes the SUT engine wrote over the window (v5.17+, celeris#585); same delta rule as zc_sends_submitted.

ring_bytes_fraction.description: ring_bytes / (inline_bytes + ring_bytes) (v5.17+, celeris#585). Null when either is null or both are 0.

resourcePoint.description: One downsampled sample in a resourceStats.series. ts_unix is the observer's unix-second timestamp; metric leaves are nullable.
